heading: Agenda
text:
## Agenda [IRET.11]

An **activation** is a matched rule waiting to fire: which rule, which
token satisfied it, when the match was made, and whether it has already
fired.

| Field | Holds |
|---|---|
| rule | the terminal whose LHS matched |
| token | the match itself |
| creation_timetag | when the match was made — the SECOND key, within one rule |
| fired | whether this activation has already fired |

Ordering comes from two places and never from arrival: the activation's
terminal ordinal ([IRET.8]) is the first key, and the creation timetag
orders the activations of ONE rule against each other ([LDET.5.4], [LDET.5.5]).

**Refraction is the flag on the activation.** A fired activation stays on its
terminal's list, carrying the flag, and is not selected again while its match
lasts ([IDAT.6.2.2]), so asking whether a match has fired cannot drift out of
step with the activation it describes. Two per-terminal structures back the
flag where a match is formed again without having ended: the refraction table
([IRET.11.3]) and the edge-once set for clock-driven matches ([IRET.11.3.5]).
The identity both key on is the (rule, token) pair — see [IRET.11.3.3] for why
the token's fact-id tuple, and not its hash, is what makes that identity safe.

idris.name: Iret_11__tok
idris.note: The clause's activation: the rule is the table the token sits in, the token is the bound facts, the creation timetag is the position in that table (tokens are appended in creation order and never reordered), `refracted` is `fired`.

idris.name: Iret_8_1__act
idris.note: The activation of the agenda: the match, and refraction as a flag on it, as the clause's header has it.

idris.name: iret_11__acts_at_ext
idris.note: The activations at an ordinal depend on the chains' activations alone: extensionality the quiet-tick proof needs.

idris.name: iret_11__chain_acts_at
idris.note: The activations of the chain at an ordinal; none past the chains.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__tables_agree_at
idris.note: Under the tables' agreement, the unblocked tokens of the table at an ordinal are the activations of the chain at it.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer
idris.note: THE TRANSFER THEOREM: run on one history from the loaded network and from FireLoop's empty state under the program the network lowers to, the two engines reach one working memory, and each table's unblocked tokens are its terminal's activations, in order and with their flags. Against the plain pipeline, inputs without Rete/PumpBoundary.idr's TMS phase and without the clock; Rete/NetworkTmsTransfer.idr carries the phase and Rete/NetworkTtl.idr the clock, on this agreement.

idris.name: Rlow_4_2_1__tables_agree
idris.note: Each table's unblocked tokens are the corresponding terminal's activations, in order and with their `fired` flags.

idris.name: iret_11__to_act
idris.note: A FireLoop token as the activation the network holds: the match and whether it fired.

idris.name: iret_11__to_acts
idris.note: Tokens as activations; named so that no statement mentions the conversion unapplied.

idris.name: iret_11__table_at_nth
idris.note: The r-th table, when the rule and table lists line up.
